title: Home page opens and names the product
expected: The page title and the first heading are both "Acme Tasks", and the today counter (data-testid="today-counter") is on the page.

title: Today counter reaches the number of open tasks
steps: Open GET / and read the today counter repeatedly from the moment the page loads until it stops changing.
expected: The counter starts at 0, shows the numbers in between, and comes to rest on the number of open tasks.

title: Today counter counts up without flicker
steps: Not automated: whether the count-up reads as a smooth climb rather than a flicker or a visible jump is a human-eye judgement, and an assertion on it would only re-measure the numbers TB-002 already checks. Open GET / and watch the counter for its first second.
expected: The counter climbs from 0 to the number of open tasks over about 600 ms, with no flicker and no skipped step.

title: Task list shows every task
expected: All five seeded tasks are listed, and the two that have no due date are shown as having none.

title: Task list filters to the open tasks
expected: Every task listed has status open, and the done task is not listed.

title: Task list filters to the done tasks
expected: Every task listed has status done, and the open tasks are not listed.

title: Task list sorts by due date with undated tasks last
expected: The tasks that have a due date come first in ascending date order, and every task with no due date comes after all of them.

title: Task detail page shows one task
expected: The page shows that task's title, its status and its due date.

title: Unknown task id gives a 404 page
steps: Open GET /tasks/999, an id no task has.
expected: The response status is 404 and the body is an HTML page, not a JSON error.

title: Notification settings page offers a test email
expected: The page shows a "Send a test email" button.

title: Test email reaches the recipient
steps: Open GET /settings/notifications and press "Send a test email".
expected: The test email is sent and the page reports that it was sent. This is the product's specified behaviour. This demo has no mail transport, so the case is red here; it is declared in known-reds.yml with that reason and is not rewritten to expect the failure.

title: Task API returns every task
expected: 200 with the five seeded tasks as JSON; the two without a due date have due null.

title: Task API filters by status
expected: Each response contains only the tasks with the status asked for.

title: Task API sorts by due date with undated tasks last
expected: The tasks with a due date come first in ascending order, and every task whose due is null comes after all of them.

title: Task API returns one task
expected: 200 with that task's id, title, status and due.

title: Task API rejects an unknown id
steps: GET /api/tasks/999, an id no task has.
expected: 404 with the JSON body {"error":"not found"}.

title: Task API creates a task
expected: The task is created, comes back with an id and status open, and appears in GET /api/tasks.

title: Task API requires a title
steps: POST /api/tasks with no title at all, then POST /api/tasks with a title of only spaces.
expected: Both are 400 with the JSON body {"error":"title is required"}.

title: Task API changes a task's status
steps: PATCH /api/tasks/:id with status done, then PATCH the same task with status open.
expected: Each call succeeds and the task's status afterwards is the one that was sent.

title: Task API rejects a status that is neither open nor done
expected: 400, and the task's status is left as it was.

title: Test email endpoint reports that there is no mail transport
expected: 503 with the JSON body {"error":"mail transport unavailable"}. The contract specifies this for this demo, so unlike TB-011 this case is green.

title: Version endpoint reports the version under test
steps: GET /version on a freshly started app.
expected: 200 with a JSON body whose version is the seeded semver 1.4.0 and whose build is 12 hexadecimal characters.

title: Simulated redeployment changes the version under test
steps: Out of the regression scope: POST /__admin/deploy is not part of the product surface but the test hook the quality gate uses to create a redeployment in the middle of a run, and the gate's own self-tests exercise it. Automating it in this suite would also move the version under a running unit and make the gate report INCONCLUSIVE on a healthy run.
expected: POST /__admin/deploy with a semver body makes GET /version report that version and a new build id.
